title: Drosophila DNp03 descending neurons serve as a hub within a flight saccade network.
source_locator: Results, 'Unilateral DNp03 activation drives saccades...'; Fig. 4A-F; Video S1
quote: When we unilaterally activated DNp03, flies increased the ipsilateral WBA and decreased the contralateral WBA
mapping_basis: The paper's name DNp03 is a MANC/Namiki type name listed in type_list.csv; the driver SS01559 maps to DNp03 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 627 nm LED aimed at the thorax, 100 ms, 29.5 mW/cm2 at the fly; three trials per fly
type_coverage: one of the two DNp03 neurons (stochastic FLP-out; bilateral expression was rare, about 2%)
sensory_condition: tethered flight, glued to a tungsten rod at about 30 degrees, near-IR illumination, high-speed video from above
coordination_notes: fictive saccade: ipsilateral wing beat amplitude up, contralateral down, plus a head turn away from the activated side
n_flies_note: right DNp03 n = 21 trials (7 flies); left DNp03 n = 18 trials (6 flies); negative control n = 18 trials (6 flies)
notes: Flight experiment: only wing beat amplitudes and head yaw were tracked (SLEAP), so the legs are not described under activation and all leg-rhythm fields are not_assessed per PROTOCOL sec. 3 (wing/flight behaviours). The paper's leg-extension scoring (Fig. 7G) belongs to looming-stimulus and silencing experiments, not to an activation experiment. Genetically matched negative controls (no CsChrimson in either DNp03) showed no change, so red light alone did not cause turning.

title: Drosophila DNp03 descending neurons serve as a hub within a flight saccade network.
source_locator: Results, 'Bilateral DNp03 activation drives wing, head, and body motions of a saccade'; Fig. 6A-D; Video S4
quote: bilateral activation resulted in an increase in both WBAs (Figure 6B, D, Video S4)
mapping_basis: The paper's name DNp03 is a MANC/Namiki type name listed in type_list.csv; CsChrimson was driven by the DNp03 split-GAL4 SS01559, which maps to DNp03 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 627 nm LED aimed at the thorax, 100 ms, 29.5 mW/cm2 at the fly; three trials per fly
sensory_condition: tethered flight, near-IR illumination, high-speed video from above at 3000 frames/s
coordination_notes: both wing beat amplitudes increased; the absolute right minus left WBA showed a trending but non-significant increase (p = 0.34)
n_flies_note: DNp03 n = 27 trials (9 flies); no-retinal control n = 27 trials (9 flies)
notes: Flight experiment: only wing beat amplitudes were tracked, the legs are not described, so leg-rhythm fields are not_assessed per PROTOCOL sec. 3 (wing/flight behaviours). Control was the same genotype reared without retinal.

title: Drosophila DNp03 descending neurons serve as a hub within a flight saccade network.
source_locator: Results, 'Bilateral DNp03 activation drives wing, head, and body motions of a saccade'; Fig. 6E-M; Video S5
quote: We found dual DNp03 activation increased the wing stroke amplitudes (WSA) of both wings (Figure 6G)
mapping_basis: The paper's name DNp03 is a MANC/Namiki type name listed in type_list.csv; CsChrimson was driven by the DNp03 split-GAL4 SS01559, which maps to DNp03 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: collimated 625 nm red LED, 100 ms bout triggered when the fly entered the centre of the chamber
sensory_condition: free flight in a transparent chamber; three orthogonal high-speed cameras at 8000 frames/s with near-IR backlights
coordination_notes: both wing stroke amplitudes increased while the absolute right minus left WSA also increased, indicating turning; flies pitched up and increased roll and yaw
n_flies_note: DNp03 n = 103 trials (50 flies); empty split-GAL4 (SS01062) control n = 48 trials (53 flies)
notes: Free-flight experiment: a 12 degree-of-freedom hull reconstruction gave body and wing kinematics only; the legs are not described, so leg-rhythm fields are not_assessed per PROTOCOL sec. 3 (wing/flight behaviours). Separate record from the tethered bilateral activation (Fig. 6B-D) because the preparation differs.

title: MDN brain descending neurons coordinately activate backward and inhibit forward locomotion.
source_locator: Results, 'MDNs persist through metamorphosis and induce backward walking in adults'; Fig. 8C,D,F; Video 5; Methods 'Adult behavioral intersectional experiment (Figure 8C,D,F)'
quote: We observed light-induced backward walking in 8 of 10 adult flies assayed (Figure 8D; Video 5)
mapping_basis: The paper names the neurons MDNs (adult moonwalker descending neurons), which is the MANC type name MDN (synonym DNp50) in type_list.csv; expression was additionally restricted by the adult MDN line VT044845-lexA, an MDN hemidriver in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 0.28 mW/mm2 red light for 10 s after 10 s dark, three times per fly
sensory_condition: wings clipped; agar ring arena (1.4 cm outer / 1.0 cm inner diameter); low transmitted light; video at 5 Hz
other_cell_types: unidentified off-target neuron with a projection not connected to the MDNs (green-line arbor, Fig. 8F)
penetrance: 8 of 10 flies walked backward; backward-walking probability within 2 s of light about 0.7 vs about 0.1 in controls (Fig. 8D, p<0.0001)
n_flies_note: 10 experimental adults; the 2 non-responders lacked ReaChR in moonwalker neurons
notes: Intersectional FLP-out: Split3 (larval MDN line, no adult central-brain expression) drives UAS-FLP, which unlocks lexAop-FRT-stop-FRT-ReaChR under the adult MDN line VT044845-lexA. Outcome is backward walking, scored by eye from 5 Hz video as the probability of starting backward walking within 2 s of light onset; no leg tracking. Coded under PROTOCOL sec. 3 'walking forward or backward: yes for all three leg pairs'. Confidence is medium because legs were not tracked. effect_on_walking is not_assessed because the paper reports initiation of backward walking, not a change in ongoing walking.

title: MDN brain descending neurons coordinately activate backward and inhibit forward locomotion.
source_locator: Results, 'MDNs persist through metamorphosis and induce backward walking in adults'; Fig. 8G-I; Methods 'Adult behavior immortalization with RU486 experiment (Figure 8G-I)'
quote: all grew into adults that showed Chrimson-induced backward walking (n = 20; Figure 8H)
mapping_basis: The paper names the neurons MDNs and shows they match adult moonwalker neuron morphology; MDN is the MANC type name (synonym DNp50) in type_list.csv.
sensory_condition: single fly in a 10 ml serological pipette (walking assay)
other_cell_types: a few additional unidentified neurons (four off-target neurons in the example of Fig. 8I)
penetrance: all 20 adults walked backward; backward-walking probability 1.0 vs about 0.1 in no-RU486 controls (Fig. 8H, p<0.001)
n_flies_note: adults were preselected as larvae that crawled backward on Chrimson activation; 5 were stained and all showed expression in moonwalker neurons
notes: Immortalization genetics: Split1 drives RU486-inducible hPR:FLP in first-instar larvae, giving permanent Actin5C>lexA in MDNs and lexAop-CsChrimson expression (the paper writes 'Chrimson'). Each stained brain also had a few extra neurons, but only the MDNs were present in all brains. Scored as the probability of starting backward walking within 2 s of light, without leg tracking. Coded under PROTOCOL sec. 3 'walking forward or backward: yes for all three leg pairs'. Because flies were preselected on the larval phenotype, penetrance is not an unbiased estimate.
